nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, we use the mathematical concept of ``Kaluza-Klein space'', which is well-established in the mathematics and mathematical physics literature (see, for example, ). Such spaces were initially defined and studied in the context of mathematical foundations of Kaluza-Klein theories, which arise by reducing a higher-dimensional theory of gravity on such a manifold. In the present paper, such spaces are used merely as convenient auxiliary mathematical data which parameterize a GESM theory, despite the historical context in which they were introduced initially. Throughout the paper, no reduction of any putative higher dimensional theory on such spaces is ever suggested or performed.

Given $(g_\alpha,s_\alpha,\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_\alpha)\in \mathbf{Conf}_{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}}(U_\alpha)$, we set:
\begin{equation*}
\mathfrak{C}_{\alpha}(g_{\alpha},s_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_{\alpha})\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} (g_{\alpha},\varphi^\alpha,\mathcal{V}^\alpha)~~,
\end{equation*}
where $\varphi^\alpha$ and $\mathcal{V}_\alpha$ are defined as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item As explained in Subsection \ref{spectrivgauge}, the special
  trivializing atlas $(U_\alpha,\mathbf{q}_\alpha)$ is underlined by a
  special trivializing atlas $(U_\alpha,q_\alpha)$ of the fiber bundle
  $\pi:E\rightarrow M$, whose trivializing maps are diffeomorphisms
  $q_\alpha:E_\alpha\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)\rightarrow
  E_\alpha^0=U_\alpha\times \mathcal{M}$. This allows us to define smooth maps
  $\varphi^{\alpha}\in \mathcal{C}^\infty(U_\alpha,\mathcal{M})$ such that
  $s_\alpha=q_\alpha^{-1}\circ \mathrm{graph}(\varphi^\alpha)$ as in
  Subsection \ref{subsec:sigmaUfold}:
\begin{equation*}
\varphi^{\alpha}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \hat{q}_{\alpha}\circ s_{\alpha} = \mathrm{ungraph}(q_\alpha\circ s_\alpha)=p^{0}_{\alpha}\circ q_{\alpha}\circ s_{\alpha}~~.
\end{equation*}
\item As explained in Subsection \ref{spectrivgauge}, the maps
  $\mathbf{q}_\alpha:(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_\alpha, \boldsymbol{\omega}_\alpha, \mathbf{D}_\alpha,
  \mathbf{J}_\alpha)\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow}
  (\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\omega}^0_{\alpha}, \mathbf{D}^0_{\alpha},
  \mathbf{J}^0_{\alpha})=(\mathcal{S}^{p_\alpha^0}, \omega^{p_\alpha^0},
  D^{p_\alpha^0}, J^{p_\alpha^0})$ are unbased isomorphisms of
  electromagnetic structures which linearize the diffeomorphisms
  $q_\alpha$. They induce isomorphisms:
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{q}_\alpha^{(s_\alpha)}:(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}_\alpha^{s_\alpha}, \boldsymbol{\omega}_\alpha^{s_\alpha}, \mathbf{D}_\alpha^{s_\alpha},
\mathbf{J}_\alpha^{s_\alpha})\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow}
(\mathcal{S}^{\varphi^{\alpha}}, \omega^{\varphi^{\alpha}}, D^{\varphi^{\alpha}},
J^{\varphi^{\alpha}})\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathcal{D}^{\varphi^\alpha}\, ,
\end{equation*}
where we noticed that
$(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^0_{\alpha})^{s_\alpha}=(\mathcal{S}^{p^0_{\alpha}})^{s_\alpha}=\mathcal{S}^{\varphi^\alpha}$ and
we used the fact that the horizontal part of $\mathbf{D}^0_{\alpha}$ is the
trivial flat connection. This allows us to identify $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_\alpha$ with the
$\mathcal{S}^{\varphi^{\alpha}}$-valued two-form defined on $U_\alpha$
through:
\begin{equation}
\label{cVlocdef}
\mathcal{V}^{\alpha}\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} \mathbf{q}_\alpha^{(s_\alpha)}(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_\alpha)\in \Omega^2(U_\alpha,\mathcal{S}^{\varphi^{\alpha}})\, .
\end{equation}
The relation $J^{\varphi^{\alpha}}\circ
\mathbf{q}_\alpha^{(s_\alpha)}=\mathbf{q}_\alpha^{(s_\alpha)} \circ \mathbf{J}_\alpha^{s_\alpha}$ implies:
\begin{equation}
\label{eomcorresp}
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_\alpha\in \Omega^{2+,s_\alpha}_{g_\alpha, \boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}^{s_\alpha}_{\alpha},\mathbf{J}^{s_\alpha}_{\alpha}}(U_\alpha)~~\mathrm{iff}~~ \mathcal{V}^{\alpha}\in \Omega^{2+,\varphi^{\alpha}}_{g_{\alpha},\mathcal{S}^{\varphi^{\alpha}},J^{\varphi^{\alpha}}}(U_\alpha)~~
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}

The fact that $\mathfrak{C}_\alpha$ is bijective follows immediately
from its definition.  The fact that $\mathfrak{C}_{\alpha}$ induces a
bijection between solution sets follows from the equivalences:
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{equiv}
& \mathcal{E}^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}}_{E}(g_{\alpha},s_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_{\alpha}) = 0\Leftrightarrow \mathcal{E}^{\mathcal{D}}_{E}(g_{\alpha},\phi^\alpha,\mathcal{V}_\alpha)=0~~,~~\mathcal{E}^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}}_{S}(g_{\alpha},s_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_{\alpha}) = 0\Leftrightarrow 
\mathcal{E}^{\mathcal{D}}_{S}(g_{\alpha},\phi^\alpha,\mathcal{V}_\alpha)=0 \nonumber \\ 
& \mathcal{E}^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{D}}}_{K}(g_{\alpha},s_{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\mathcal{V}}_{\alpha}) = 0\Leftrightarrow \mathcal{E}^{\mathcal{D}}_{K}(g_{\alpha},\phi^\alpha,\mathcal{V}_\alpha)=0~~.
\end{eqnarray}
This follows by a direct but somewhat lengthy computation using
relations \eqref{eomcorresp}, which we will not reproduce here. For
example, it is easy to see that the relation

Let $h$ be a pseudo-Riemannian metric on $E$ and $g$ be a
pseudo-Riemannian metric on $M$. Then the following statements are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[1.]
\item $h$ is compatible with $\pi$ and $g$, i.e. we have $h\in
  \mathrm{Met}_{\pi,g}(E)$.
\item $h$ is vertically non-degenerate with respect to $\pi$ and
  coincides with the Kaluza-Klein metric determined by $H\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} H(h)$,
  $g$ and by the metric $h_V\stackrel{{\rm def.}}{=} h|_{V}\in \mathrm{Met}(V)$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $h$ is uniquely determined by $H(h)$, $g$ and $h_V$.
